title: PayFair: EU pay-transparency kit for companies with 20–250 staff
summary: The EU Pay Transparency Directive gives every worker the right to ask about pay levels, bans questions about salary history and requires pay ranges for candidates. Big compensation tools cost thousands a year. PayFair helps small employers set job levels and pay ranges, answer pay-information requests on time and keep job ads compliant.
hook: "An employee asked for the average pay of her role by gender. We have 40 staff and no HR system. What are we supposed to send?"
story:
**Marta is the office manager of a 45-person engineering firm in Warsaw.** Poland's first pay-transparency rules took effect in December 2025: candidates must be told the pay or pay range, job adverts must be gender-neutral, and the firm can no longer ask about past salaries. When the full directive is transposed, any employee can ask for **average pay levels by gender for their category of work**, with a deadline to answer.

The firm has never defined job levels. Salaries were set one by one. A compensation platform quoted **several thousand euros a year**, far too much. Marta needs a simple way to group roles, set ranges, check job ads and produce an answer to a pay request in an afternoon.
whyNow: The transposition deadline was 7 June 2026. Only a few member states had fully transposed by then, but Poland, Belgium, Czechia and Malta have partial rules in force and others are drafting. Rules on candidates and the right to information apply to employers of all sizes, while big tools are priced for companies with 250+ staff.
evidence: Only four member states (Italy, Slovakia, Lithuania, Malta) had fully transposed the directive by late June 2026; Sweden sought a postponement [WageIndicator / King & Spalding]
Poland's recruitment rules took effect on 24 December 2025: pay information for candidates, gender-neutral adverts and no questions on past earnings [Lewis Silkin / RSM Poland]
Employers must answer pay-information requests within two months under the directive; Poland gives 30 days [Trusaic]
Ravio's pricing page gives £5,400 a year as an example for a 250-person company [Ravio]
Lattice charges $6 per user for compensation with a $4,000 annual minimum [FirstHR]

solution.title: Import salaries
solution.text: upload a payroll export (CSV); names can be replaced by IDs.

solution.title: Group roles
solution.text: AI suggests categories of "work of equal value" from job titles and short descriptions, using skills, effort, responsibility and working conditions; the owner adjusts.

solution.title: Set ranges
solution.text: PayFair suggests a pay range per level and flags people outside it and gender gaps per category.

solution.title: Answer requests
solution.text: when an employee asks, PayFair produces the answer letter with the right averages and tracks the deadline.

solution.title: Check job ads
solution.text: paste a job advert to check pay range, neutral wording and banned questions for that country.

must: Pay-information request letters with deadline tracking

techStack: LLM for job grouping and ad checks

timeline.what: **Validate, no code.** Interview 15 SMEs and 5 recruiters in Poland and one more early country; build one pay structure by hand.
Import, job grouping, ranges and gap view.
Request letters, job-ad checker, country rule packs.
